title: Blueprint Farm Choreography — Storyline, Dependency Graph, Release Slices
page0: Choreograph the Blueprint Farm and software-factory upgrades into a sequence that feels like a coherent storyline rather than a pile of projects. Ask open questions before locking answers. Build dependency-safe implementation slices, make each slice independently useful, and preserve the ability to stop after any slice without leaving the system half-broken. Execute only Slice 1 now.
correctedQuestion: What sequence of reversible, independently valuable slices yields the most information and compounding capability per unit of risk, while preserving production stability and making each later upgrade easier to execute with the machinery built earlier?
objective: Create the release storyline that turns blueprint production, maintenance truth, deterministic generation, worker orchestration and the 3D factory into one cumulative manufacturing system.

knownEvidence.claim: Core manufacturing stations and quality law already exist conceptually and partly in runtime.
A spatial observability surface already exists.
Blueprint and law assets can already be indexed for retrieval.

openQuestions: Which early slice most reduces ambiguity for every later slice?
Which later capabilities depend on real production data that does not yet exist and therefore should not be built early?
Where can a slice be made useful to humans before automation exists?
Which slices require owner policy decisions that should be deferred until the system can present better evidence?
What is the smallest end-to-end demonstration that proves Blueprint → release → worker → QC → factory visibility without overbuilding?
Which generator integrations would create the broadest reuse across UI, worlds and environments?
What measures indicate the Blueprint Farm is improving throughput rather than creating planning bureaucracy?
At what point does 3D visualization become valuable enough to expand beyond current Citadel state?
Which maintenance debt should be removed before adding worker automation?
How should the storyline adapt when another chat lands overlapping infrastructure during implementation?
assumptions: The repo remains concurrently edited by multiple chats/workers.
Slices should prefer additive contracts and registries before invasive runtime rewrites.
A later slice can be re-planned if evidence changes; the choreography is versioned, not destiny.
v44 remains production authority unless separately promoted.
nonGoals: Do not schedule dates or promise background execution.
Do not auto-release the next slice after one passes.
Do not make visual polish a prerequisite for core authority correctness.
Do not block useful existing workflows while future architecture is being built.

storyline.purpose: Make plans inspectable and cumulative before adding more automation.
storyline.humanExperience: You can see every major future blueprint, what it depends on, what is still unknown and what is safe to build next.

storyline.purpose: Measure and simplify current Funnel machinery before asking it to orchestrate more work.
storyline.humanExperience: The factory stops relying on mythology; every machine has a job, evidence and maintenance state.

storyline.act: ACT III — Give the factory reproducible materials
storyline.purpose: Standardize deterministic procedural recipes and generator capability resolution.
storyline.humanExperience: A blueprint can say what it wants generated and MOOR knows which existing tool can reproducibly make it.

storyline.purpose: Translate one selected blueprint slice into a scoped, traceable execution release.
storyline.humanExperience: You choose one slice; the system creates a precise job packet without beginning unrelated work.

storyline.act: ACT V — Open the work cells
storyline.purpose: Connect actual workers only after scope, reuse and stale-state controls exist.
storyline.humanExperience: Parallel workers build isolated pieces, an integration cell recombines them, and QC independently proves the integrated result.

storyline.act: ACT VI — Make the machine visible
storyline.purpose: Drive the 3D factory from real snapshots, work orders and maintenance state.
storyline.humanExperience: Walking through the factory shows what the software is actually doing, not decorative motion.

storyline.act: ACT VII — Decide what becomes law
storyline.purpose: Use accumulated maintenance/performance evidence to decide whether any candidate authority should be promoted.
storyline.humanExperience: Promotion and further automation become informed owner decisions rather than architectural momentum.

releaseSlices.name: Blueprint Farm Registry + Pulse Library
releaseSlices.stopState: Useful standalone planning library even if no later slice is built.

releaseSlices.name: Blueprint comparison / unresolved-question inspector
releaseSlices.stopState: Human can choose what to resolve next without worker automation.

decisionPolicy.nextSlice: Never automatic. Present currently eligible slices, unresolved questions, expected information gain, risk and dependency state.
decisionPolicy.concurrency: Only independent slices with explicit non-overlapping authority/write scope may run concurrently.

interfaces.contract: Read blueprint versions, open questions and slice DAG.
Propose next slice; Funnel/owner decides release.
Update slice eligibility and rework state; never auto-release next work.

failureModes.containment: Version choreography and re-evaluate after material evidence.
Each release has explicit scope/done criteria; new work becomes a new slice.
Dependency must name a concrete required output/evidence, not vague sequencing preference.
Every slice must leave a valid stop state.
3D expansion waits for real data contracts unless it is purely decorative.

maintenanceModel.updateRule: Revise when a slice changes dependency/interface assumptions or when verified evidence changes eligibility.

observability.human: Pulse shows the acts, current slice, eligible next slices, blocked reasons and unresolved questions.
observability.machine: Farm index stores the DAG and statuses.
observability.factory: Future floor can light only released/active slices; planned slices appear as blueprint/archive objects, not fake running machinery.

securityAuthority.release: Explicit owner/Funnel decision required per slice.
securityAuthority.promotion: Authority promotion remains a separate critical slice.
securityAuthority.plannedState: A planned slice has no execution authority.

implementationSlices.name: Eligibility calculator
implementationSlices.deliverable: Determine eligible/blocked slices from evidence; read-only.

implementationSlices.name: Release UI
implementationSlices.deliverable: Human can explicitly release one eligible slice.

acceptance: Every major future build maps to a slice with explicit dependencies and a valid stop state.
Only BF-01 is marked buildNow in this version.
The storyline explains why each act exists without making chronology a substitute for evidence.
Open questions can block or redirect slices.
No next slice auto-releases after completion.
Concurrent work is permitted only when dependency and ownership contracts allow it.
rollback: The choreography is a versioned planning artifact. Reverting to a prior choreography never mutates already released artifacts or authority records.
